To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the probability of developing cancer during life-time is increasing and that the probability of dying of cancer during life-time has not changed significantly.
in the population of Saalnd in 1980, a man has a 32.4% probability of eventually developing a malignancy, a woman a 29.7% probability.
the probability at birth for men and women of developing a malignant neoplasms increased from 24% and 25% in 1971 to 32% and 30%, respectively, in 1985.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to describe the cancer burden in a given population, which is of particular relevance to the planning and evaluation of cancer-control programs and to the assessment of their impact.
the life-time risk as a measure for the cancer burden in a given population, which is of importance for cancer control.
the life-time risk as a measure of the burden of cancer in the population and its time-trend.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the probability at birth to eventually develop a malignant neoplsm increased in Saarland between 1970-72 and 1980/1985, and that the life-time risk was highest for lung, breast, colorectal and prostate cancer.
life-time risks are increasing in the population of Saaraand.
the risk of developing cancer is higher today than it was 15 years ago, but that this statement is not valid for all age-groups, for all cancer types, and for all countries or regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
life-time risks are useful for the assessment of cancer risks and their changes over time.
, for most forms of cancer, the life-time risk has increased during the past two decades in Saarland.

, with respect to the probability of developing cancer, a substantial increase has been observed in the population of Saalnd, Germany in the last 15 years, and that this increase is mainly due to the increase in life expectancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

life-time risk estimates provide a more complete description of the cancer burden than the cumulative rate, and that the life-time risk is a better indicator for the cancer risk of a population than the cumulative rate.

the probability of developing a cancer during life-time is a more comprehensive measure of the cancer problem than any of the commonly used descriptive epidemiological parameters, and that the life-time risk is the only one which allows for a direct comparison of cancer risks between different countries or different time periods.
the life-time risk is the most important single measure of cancer burden in a given population.
